info.title: Localtonet API v2
info.description:
## Localtonet API v2

API for managing tunnels, authentication tokens, token groups, and per-tunnel configuration.
All endpoints require a **Bearer API key** obtain yours from the [Localtonet Dashboard](https://localtonet.com/dashboard).


---

### Tunnels
Create, retrieve, start, stop, and delete tunnels. Supports all tunnel types:
- **HTTP** random subdomain, custom subdomain, or your own verified domain
- **TCP / UDP / TCP+UDP** raw socket tunnels with optional port reservation
- **HTTP Proxy / SOCKS5 Proxy** route outbound traffic through your local machine
- **Shared / Rotating Proxy** distribute connections across multiple client credentials for IP rotation

Bulk endpoints (up to 100 items per request) are available for create, start, stop, and delete operations.


---

### Authentication Tokens
Tokens identify Localtonet clients (devices). For each token you can:
- List all tunnels running under that token
- View the public IP change history of the device
- Configure **airplane-mode automation** (mobile IP rotation)
- Register **change-IP** and **restart-device** webhook trigger links
- Set default command-line arguments inherited by all tunnels under the token


---

### Token Groups
Organise tokens into named groups (e.g. *"Office Devices"*, *"Android Pool"*).
Groups can be assigned to Shared Proxy tunnels to enable multi-device IP rotation.
Tokens can belong to multiple groups simultaneously.


---

### Tunnel Configuration
Fine-grained per-tunnel settings:
| Category | What you can do |
|---|---|
| **IP Restrictions** | Whitelist or blacklist IP addresses / CIDR ranges |
| **Access Controls** | Whitelist or blacklist URL paths / wildcard patterns |
| **Custom Headers** | Inject request & response HTTP headers |
| **Authentication** | Enable HTTP Basic Auth with custom credentials |
| **Expiration** | Auto-stop a tunnel at a scheduled UTC date/time |
| **Server Port** | Change the public port for TCP/UDP tunnels |
| **Rate Limit** | Cap upload/download speed (B/s, KB/s, MB/s) |
| **Bandwidth Limit** | Set a total data quota; tunnel stops when reached |
| **Bandwidth Usage** | View cumulative usage and reset the counter |
| **Arguments** | Pass advanced CLI arguments to the Localtonet client |
| **Shared Proxy Clients** | Add, update, and remove per-client credentials, bandwidth limits, thread limits, and expiration dates |


---

### Servers
Retrieve available server locations and their codes.
Use the returned `serverCode` when creating tunnels to choose your preferred region.


---

get.description: Retrieves all authentication tokens for the authenticated user. Each token represents a device or deployment slot and can be used to authenticate Localtonet clients and create tunnels.

post.description: Creates a new authentication token. Use this token to authenticate the Localtonet client on a device. The raw token value is returned only at creation time � store it securely.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific authentication token including its name, creation date, associated tunnel count, online status, and device settings.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an authentication token. All tunnels associated with this token are immediately stopped and deleted. This action cannot be undone.

get.description: Retrieves all tunnels associated with a specific authentication token. Useful for monitoring all active or configured tunnels on a particular device.

get.summary: Get IP History By Auth Token
get.description: Retrieves the public IP address change history for a specific authentication token. Tracks every IP change event with a timestamp. Append ?view=summary for a quick overview showing only the current IP and total change count.

Retrieves the automatic airplane mode settings configured for the device using this authentication token. Airplane mode automation periodically toggles mobile connectivity to force a public IP change.

patch.description: Configures automatic airplane mode scheduling for the mobile device using this token. When enabled, the Localtonet mobile client periodically toggles airplane mode to rotate the device's public IP. Ideal for mobile proxy rotation setups.

post.description: Registers a webhook trigger link under the specified airplane mode setting. The Localtonet client calls this URL to initiate an IP address rotation (e.g., rebooting a router or toggling a mobile gateway).

delete.description: Removes a previously registered change-IP webhook trigger link. The Localtonet client will no longer call this URL during IP rotation.

post.description: Registers a webhook trigger link that the Localtonet client calls to remotely reboot the device running the client (mobile phone, router, or server). Attached to the specified airplane mode setting.

delete.description: Removes a previously registered device-restart webhook trigger link. The Localtonet client will no longer call this URL when a device reboot is scheduled.

get.description: Retrieves the default command-line arguments associated with this authentication token. These arguments are inherited by all tunnels created under this token unless overridden at the tunnel level.

patch.description: Configures the default command-line arguments for all tunnels using this authentication token. Newly created tunnels inherit these arguments. Useful for applying Docker networking or IP binding defaults globally.

get.description: Retrieves all available server locations for tunnel creation. Returns server codes, geographic locations, supported protocols, and availability status. Use the server codes when creating tunnels to choose your preferred location. Results are cached for 5 minutes.
Retrieves all SSO providers configured for the authenticated user.

post.description: Creates a new SSO provider or updates an existing one. Supply the `Id` field to update an existing provider. Omit it to create a new one.

get.description: Retrieves the default OAuth2/OIDC endpoint URLs and callback path for a given SSO provider type (e.g. Google, GitHub, Microsoft).

delete.description: Soft-deletes the specified SSO provider. The provider will no longer be available for use in tunnels.

get.description: Retrieves the SSO configuration for a specific tunnel, including which providers are enabled and access control settings.

put.description: Configures which SSO providers are active for a given tunnel and sets access control rules such as allowed email domains, usernames, and SSO paths.

get.description: Retrieves all token groups owned by the authenticated user. Each group includes its name and the number of member tokens. Token groups are used to organize devices and can be assigned to shared-proxy tunnels for IP rotation.

post.description: Creates a new token group. Groups are useful for organizing authentication tokens by location (e.g., 'Office Devices'), purpose (e.g., 'Production'), or device type (e.g., 'Android Phones'). Groups can also be assigned to shared-proxy tunnels to enable IP rotation across the group's tokens.

get.description: Retrieves a specific token group by its ID, including the full list of authentication tokens that are members of the group (token name, value, and online status).

delete.description: Permanently deletes a token group and all its membership associations. The authentication tokens that were members of the group remain active and unaffected.

post.description: Adds an authentication token to the specified token group. A token can belong to multiple groups at the same time, enabling flexible organization by multiple criteria (e.g., by location and by purpose).

delete.description: Removes an authentication token from a token group. The token itself is unaffected and continues to function normally � it simply loses its membership in this group.

get.description: Retrieves all IP address restrictions configured for the tunnel. Use IP restrictions to whitelist (allow) or blacklist (deny) specific IP addresses or CIDR ranges from accessing the tunnel.

post.description: Adds a new IP address or CIDR range restriction to the tunnel. Supports both individual IPs (e.g., 203.0.113.45) and subnet ranges (e.g., 203.0.113.0/24). Use the PATCH endpoint to set whether the list acts as an allowlist or a blocklist.

patch.description: Sets whether the IP restriction list operates as an allowlist (whitelist) or a blocklist (blacklist). This applies globally to all IP entries on the tunnel.

delete.description: Removes every IP restriction entry from the tunnel in a single operation. After this call the tunnel accepts connections from all IP addresses. This action cannot be undone.
Removes a single IP address or CIDR range entry from the tunnel's IP restriction list.

get.description: Retrieves all URL path access control entries configured for the tunnel. Access controls restrict which URL paths can be reached through the tunnel, supporting both exact paths and wildcard patterns.

post.description: Adds a URL path entry to the tunnel's access control list. Supports exact paths (e.g., /admin) and wildcard patterns (e.g., /api/*). Use the PATCH endpoint to configure whether the list acts as an allowlist or a blocklist.

patch.description: Sets whether the URL path access control list operates as an allowlist (whitelist) or a blocklist (blacklist). This applies globally to all URL entries on the tunnel.

delete.description: Removes every URL path access control entry from the tunnel in a single operation. After this call all paths are accessible through the tunnel. This action cannot be undone.
Removes a single URL path entry from the tunnel's access control list.

get.description: Retrieves the custom HTTP headers configured for the tunnel. Includes both request headers (injected into every request forwarded to your local server) and response headers (appended to every response sent back to clients).

patch.description: Configures custom HTTP headers injected by the tunnel proxy. Request headers are added to every request before it reaches your local server. Response headers are added to every response before it reaches the client. Example; { "X-Real-IP": "client_ip", "X-Source": "localtonet" }

get.description: Retrieves the HTTP Basic Authentication configuration for the tunnel. Shows whether authentication is active and the username currently set (password is never returned).

patch.description: Enables or disables HTTP Basic Authentication on the tunnel. When enabled, all HTTP requests must include a valid Authorization header; unauthenticated requests receive a 401 response.

get.description: Retrieves the expiration date for the tunnel. Once this date/time is reached the tunnel is automatically stopped. A null value means the tunnel has no expiration and runs indefinitely.

patch.description: Schedules an automatic stop for the tunnel at a specific UTC date and time. Pass null to remove the expiration and let the tunnel run indefinitely.

get.description: Retrieves the public server-side port that external clients connect to for a TCP/UDP tunnel. Only applicable to TCP, UDP, and TCP-UDP tunnel types.

patch.description: Changes the public server-side port for a TCP/UDP tunnel. The port is what external clients connect to. Only available for TCP, UDP, and TCP-UDP tunnel types. A tunnel restart is required for the change to take effect.

get.description: Retrieves the bandwidth rate limit (speed cap) configured for the tunnel. Separate upload and download limits can be set. A value of 0 means no speed restriction.

patch.description: Configures independent upload and download bandwidth speed caps for the tunnel. Useful for throttling heavy consumers or guaranteeing fair usage. Set a size to 0 to remove the limit for that direction. SizeTypes; 1 = B/s, 2 = KB/s, 3 = MB/s, 4 = GB/s

get.description: Retrieves the total data transfer quota for the tunnel. Once the transferred data reaches this limit the tunnel is automatically stopped. A value of 0 means no quota restriction.

patch.description: Sets a total data transfer quota for the tunnel. The tunnel is automatically stopped when the cumulative transferred data exceeds this limit, preventing unintended overages. SizeTypes; 1 = B, 2 = KB, 3 = MB, 4 = GB

get.description: Retrieves the cumulative data transfer statistics for the tunnel since it was created or since the counter was last reset. Useful for monitoring consumption against a configured bandwidth limit.

post.description: Resets the tunnel's cumulative bandwidth usage counter to zero without affecting any configured bandwidth limit. Useful when starting a new billing or monitoring period.

get.description: Retrieves the custom command-line arguments configured for this specific tunnel. These arguments are passed to the Localtonet client when the tunnel is started and override any token-level defaults.

patch.description: Configures tunnel-specific command-line arguments passed to the Localtonet client on startup. These override any token-level defaults and are intended for advanced use cases such as Docker networking or explicit IP binding. Example; --net NET_NAME --ip IP_ADDRESS

get.description: Retrieves all clients registered on a shared/rotating proxy tunnel. Each client entry includes its credentials, optional IP binding, bandwidth limit, expiration date, and current usage statistics.

post.description: Adds a new proxy client to a shared/rotating proxy tunnel. Each client gets its own credentials and can optionally have individual bandwidth quotas, thread limits, and expiration dates. The tunnel rotates incoming requests across all active clients.

patch.description: Updates credentials, limits, and other settings for an existing client on a shared/rotating proxy tunnel. Only the fields you supply are changed.

delete.description: Removes a client from a shared/rotating proxy tunnel. The client's credentials are immediately revoked and the tunnel stops routing traffic through that client's IP.

get.description: Retrieves all tunnels for the authenticated user across all authentication tokens. Returns tunnel details including status, public URL, local target, configuration, and bandwidth statistics.
Retrieves full details of a specific tunnel: configuration, current status, public URL, local target IP and port, bandwidth usage, security settings, and all applied configurations.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a tunnel and all its configuration. Running tunnels are stopped before deletion. This action cannot be undone.

post.summary: Create HTTP Tunnel with Random SubDomain
post.description: Creates a new HTTP or File Server tunnel with a randomly generated subdomain. The system picks an available subdomain automatically. Ideal for quick local development exposure or one-off sharing.

post.summary: Create HTTP Tunnel with Custom SubDomain
post.description: Creates an HTTP or File Server tunnel using a specific subdomain you choose. The subdomain must be globally unique. Ideal for stable, branded, or memorable public URLs.

post.summary: Create HTTP Tunnel with Custom Domain
post.description: Creates an HTTP or File Server tunnel using a custom domain you own. The domain must be pre-verified through DNS configuration in the Localtonet dashboard. Perfect for production-grade, white-label deployments.

Creates a TCP, UDP, or combined TCP+UDP tunnel for exposing non-HTTP services such as databases, game servers, MQTT brokers, or any raw socket service. Supports optional port reservation to guarantee the same public port after restarts.
Creates an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy tunnel. HTTP proxies handle web traffic; SOCKS5 proxies support any TCP/UDP protocol. Useful for routing outbound traffic through your local machine or network.

Creates a proxy tunnel and returns the complete connection details (host, port, protocol, and credentials) in a single response. Designed for automated setups that need immediate access to all proxy parameters.

Creates a shared/rotating proxy tunnel that distributes connections across multiple client credentials. Ideal for IP rotation pools, load balancing, or multi-user proxy access. Configure individual clients after creation.

post.summary: Bulk Create HTTP Tunnels with Random SubDomain
post.description: Creates up to 100 HTTP tunnels in a single request, each assigned a random subdomain. Ideal for batch provisioning during automated deployments or integration test setups.

post.summary: Bulk Create HTTP Tunnels with Custom SubDomain
post.description: Creates up to 100 HTTP tunnels in a single request, each with a specified custom subdomain. All requested subdomains must be globally unique and available.

post.summary: Bulk Create HTTP Tunnels with Custom Domain
post.description: Creates up to 100 HTTP tunnels on custom domains in a single request. All domains must be pre-verified via DNS before the call.
Creates up to 100 TCP/UDP tunnels in a single request. Useful for simultaneously setting up multiple database, game-server, or raw-socket endpoints.
Creates up to 100 HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy tunnels in a single request. Ideal for building large proxy pools or distributing load across multiple proxy endpoints.

post.summary: Bulk Create Proxy Tunnels with Details
post.description: Creates up to 100 proxy tunnels and returns full connection details (host, port, credentials, protocol) for each in a single response. Designed for automated proxy-pool provisioning workflows.
Creates up to 100 shared/rotating proxy tunnels in a single request. Suitable for large-scale proxy pool provisioning where each tunnel will subsequently be populated with individual clients.
Starts a stopped tunnel, making it active and reachable at its public URL or host:port. The connected Localtonet client must be online for the tunnel to become active.
Stops a running tunnel. All active connections are immediately terminated and the public URL or port becomes inaccessible. The tunnel configuration is preserved and the tunnel can be restarted later.
Starts up to 100 tunnels simultaneously. All tunnels in the list are activated in parallel. Useful for restoring a set of tunnels after maintenance or scheduled downtime.
Stops up to 100 tunnels simultaneously. All active connections on the selected tunnels are terminated in parallel. Useful for scheduled maintenance windows or emergency shutdowns.

delete.description: Permanently deletes up to 100 tunnels in a single request. Running tunnels are stopped before deletion. This action cannot be undone.

patch.description: Renames the tunnel. The title is displayed in the dashboard and included in API responses for identification. It has no effect on the tunnel's public URL or behaviour.

Changes the local IP address that the tunnel proxies traffic to. Use this when your local service moves to a different host within the network. A tunnel restart is required for the new IP to take effect.
Changes the local port that the tunnel proxies traffic to. Use this when your local service moves to a different port. A tunnel restart is required for the change to take effect.

Enables or disables port reservation for TCP/UDP tunnels. When reserved, the same public port is re-assigned each time the tunnel starts, ensuring stable external connectivity for clients that hard-code the port. Only available for TCP, UDP, and TCP+UDP tunnel types.

Enables or disables legacy connection mode. Legacy mode ensures compatibility with older Localtonet client versions at the cost of reduced performance. Only enable when required for backward compatibility.

get.description: Retrieves a list of recent HTTP requests forwarded through the tunnel. Each entry includes the HTTP method, path, response status code, response time in milliseconds, and the originating client IP. Only available for HTTP and File Server tunnels.

patch.summary: Change Protocol Type for Proxy Tunnel
patch.description: Switches the proxy protocol between HTTP Proxy (6) and SOCKS5 Proxy (7). The tunnel must be stopped before changing the protocol type. Only applicable to HTTP Proxy and SOCKS5 Proxy tunnels.

patch.summary: Bulk Change Protocol Type for Proxy Tunnels
patch.description: Changes the protocol type for multiple tunnels in a single request. All targeted tunnels must be stopped before the call. Only applicable to HTTP Proxy and SOCKS5 Proxy tunnels.

ApiKey.description: You can get ApiKey from https://localtonet.com/dashboard
